platforms.name: llama.cpp
platforms.notes: Backend table has no Gaudi/Habana entry. Tensor-parallel split mode is explicitly EXPERIMENTAL and unimplemented for most MoE/hybrid architectures (expert placement instead relies on manual --n-cpu-moe/--override-tensor flags). FP8 is not a first-class ggml dtype — it exists only as the internal scale format inside MXFP4/NVFP4 blocks. AWQ/GPTQ GGUF-conversion tooling was removed/never supported.

platforms.name: LMDeploy
platforms.notes: AMD is partial: a ROCm install path exists (LMDEPLOY_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm) but KV-cache quantization docs restrict to CUDA/Ascend and the internal device_type validator omits rocm. No CPU-only backend (device_type validator allows only cuda/ascend/maca/camb). Speculative decoding (EAGLE/EAGLE3) is explicitly labeled experimental. Also supports Moore Threads MACA and Cambricon NPU (outside this matrix's hardware keys).

platforms.name: MLX-LM
platforms.notes: MLX is no longer Apple-only: mlx core now ships an official CUDA backend for Linux/NVIDIA (pip install mlx[cuda12]) and a separate CPU-only Linux backend, alongside its original Metal/Apple-Silicon path — mlx-lm's own setup.py confirms this at the package level (extras_require cuda12/cuda13/cpu each pull in the matching mlx[...] backend, overriding the base install_requires' Darwin-only mlx dependency) — no AMD/Gaudi/Ascend backend exists in either repo. GGUF is export-only and limited to Mistral/Mixtral/Llama-style models (mlx-lm cannot load a .gguf file for inference). KV-cache quantization is integer/affine, not FP8-format.

platforms.name: Ollama
platforms.notes: Judged on Ollama's own documented behavior, not inherited llama.cpp capability. gpu.mdx (the dedicated hardware doc) covers only Nvidia/AMD-ROCm/Metal/Vulkan — no Ascend or Gaudi section. No tensor-parallel/split-mode flag is exposed; MoE expert-offload PRs are unmerged. Speculative decoding merged only on the Apple-Silicon MLX runner for specific models — the general feature request is still open. No hybrid state-space models in Ollama's library (Jamba/Mamba/Falcon-Mamba all 404 on ollama.com). nvfp4 downgraded to partial: import.mdx's own quantize docs list only q8_0/q4_K_S/q4_K_M, and NVFP4-tagged models exist on ollama.com/library (e.g. qwen3.6:27b-coding-nvfp4) but loading one hits an open, unresolved crash — issue #16056 reports `ggml.c:1676: GGML_ASSERT(type >= 0 && type < GGML_TYPE_COUNT) failed` loading an NVFP4 GGUF; the corresponding llama.cpp PR is linked but not yet ported to Ollama's fork.

platforms.name: SGLang
platforms.notes: intel_gaudi marked partial: no dedicated hardware-platform guide (overview.mdx lists only nvidia/amd/ascend/cpu/jetson/tpu/xpu), but --device accepts "hpu" and a legacy HpuCommunicator class exists (inherited from the vLLM lineage). gguf is NVIDIA+Ascend only — no AMD/ROCm (Marlin-kernel dependent).

platforms.name: TensorRT-LLM
platforms.notes: NVIDIA-only, proprietary TensorRT compiler stack — no AMD/Gaudi/ Apple/Ascend/CPU inference path in any fetched doc. Disaggregated serving is documented as mature but limited to decoder-only models at beam width 1. GGUF is never mentioned (TRT-LLM uses its own ModelOpt checkpoint/engine format).

platforms.name: Text Generation Inference (TGI)
platforms.notes: TGI is in maintenance mode as of this verification (README: only bug-fix/doc PRs accepted, recommends vLLM/SGLang/llama.cpp/MLX going forward). ep_size != 1 explicitly raises for DeepSeek-V2 (expert parallel unsupported); no pipeline-parallel or hybrid Mamba/Jamba model support found. AMD/ROCm does not support AWQ checkpoint loading.

platforms.name: vLLM
platforms.notes: Apple GPU support ships via the vllm-project-org vllm-metal plugin (MLX backend); Gaudi/Ascend likewise via official out-of-tree vllm-project plugins, not the in-tree core. GGUF requires the separate vllm-gguf-plugin. Disaggregated prefill is documented but the page itself is titled "experimental".
